# Client Backstory: Meet Sarah Chen

**Sarah Chen, 34**, is a senior software engineer at a mid-sized tech company in Seattle. Originally from Sacramento, she moved to Seattle eight years ago for her career. She is the eldest daughter of Taiwanese immigrant parents who run a small accounting firm. Sarah has a younger brother, Marcus (29), who recently got engaged. 

Sarah was in a seven-year relationship with David, an architect, that ended fourteen months ago when he left her for a colleague. They had been planning to start a family. She lives alone in a Capitol Hill apartment with her cat, Mochi. She was passed over for a promotion to engineering manager six months ago, and her best friend Priya moved to London last spring. Sarah has been seeing Dr. Martinez for four months, takes 20mg of escitalopram daily, and has a family history of depression on her mother's side. She has recently started skipping her Sunday calls with her parents.

---

## 100 Statements from Sarah During the Session

1. "I didn't want to come today, honestly. I sat in the parking garage for fifteen minutes just staring at my steering wheel."
2. "I think the medication is working, but I'm not sure if I just feel numb instead of sad now."
3. "My mom called three times yesterday and I let it go to voicemail every single time."
4. "I keep thinking about how David and I picked out names for kids we never had."
5. "There's this junior developer at work, he's maybe twenty-six, and he got the promotion I wanted."
6. "I haven't washed my hair in five days. I keep telling myself I'll do it tomorrow."
7. "Marcus sent me a save-the-date last week and I cried for two hours."
8. "I'm happy for him, I swear I am. I just don't know how to be at a wedding alone."
9. "Mochi is the only living thing I've spoken to out loud since Saturday."
10. "I had a panic attack in the Whole Foods parking lot on Tuesday and I don't even know why."
11. "My chest gets tight every Sunday night before the workweek starts."
12. "I keep replaying the conversation when David told me about Jessica."
13. "Sometimes I wonder if I drove him away by being too focused on my career."
14. "But then I think, isn't that what he said he loved about me when we met?"
15. "I miss Priya so much. The time difference makes it hard to even text."
16. "She has this whole new life in London and I'm still stuck here."
17. "I ate cereal for dinner four nights in a row last week."
18. "I bought groceries and most of them are rotting in my fridge."
19. "My manager said I seem 'checked out' in our one-on-one yesterday."
20. "I used to love coding. Now I just stare at my screen and feel nothing."
21. "I think about quitting my job almost every day, but I don't know what I'd do instead."
22. "Money isn't the issue. I have savings. But what does that even mean anymore?"
23. "I went on a date last month and I felt like I was performing being a person."
24. "He texted me afterward and I never responded. I just couldn't."
25. "My parents asked when I'm getting married last time we talked. I lied and said I was seeing someone."
26. "I don't know why I said that. Now I have to maintain this fiction."
27. "I feel like I'm thirty-four and I've failed at the basic milestones of being an adult."
28. "Everyone from college is posting babies and houses on Instagram."
29. "I deleted Instagram three weeks ago but I keep redownloading it."
30. "I lie in bed scrolling until two in the morning sometimes."
31. "Then I'm exhausted at work the next day and I hate myself for it."
32. "My doctor said the escitalopram should be at full effect by now."
33. "I'm not crying as much, but I'm not laughing either."
34. "Is feeling nothing actually better than feeling sad?"
35. "I had a dream about David last night. We were just grocery shopping. It was so mundane."
36. "I woke up and reached for him on his side of the bed."
37. "It's been fourteen months. Why am I still doing that?"
38. "My mom mentioned a friend's son at church who's 'available' and I almost screamed."
39. "She doesn't know how to ask if I'm okay. She just suggests solutions."
40. "I haven't told them I'm in therapy. They wouldn't understand."
41. "In our culture, you don't talk about this stuff. You just push through."
42. "But I can't push through anymore. I'm so tired."
43. "I forgot to pay my electric bill last month. I've never done that before."
44. "I used to be so organized. I had color-coded spreadsheets for everything."
45. "Now I can barely remember if I took my meds in the morning."
46. "I started keeping them in a pill organizer like an elderly person."
47. "I'm not suicidal, I want you to know that. But sometimes I think it would be easier to just not exist."
48. "Like, I don't want to die, I just want a break from being me."
49. "Is that something you hear a lot? Does that make sense?"
50. "I went to Marcus's engagement dinner and I drank too much wine."
51. "I made a weird comment about marriage being a 'beautiful illusion' and everyone went quiet."
52. "His fiancée, Emma, was so sweet about it. That made it worse somehow."
53. "I think my family thinks I'm bitter now. Maybe I am."
54. "I used to be the fun one. The one with all the plans."
55. "Last weekend I cancelled brunch with the only friend I have left here."
56. "I told her I was sick. I just couldn't get out of bed."
57. "She texted to check on me on Monday and I never replied."
58. "I'm pushing everyone away and I know it but I can't stop."
59. "What if I'm just becoming the person I always feared I'd become?"
60. "My grandmother had what my mom calls 'sadness sickness.' I think she had depression."
61. "She lived with us when I was little. She'd stay in bed for days."
62. "I remember being scared of her room. Now I'm becoming her."
63. "Is depression genetic? I know you've said it can be."
64. "I'm worried I'm just wired this way and nothing will actually fix me."
65. "I went into the office yesterday for the first time in two weeks."
66. "A coworker asked if I'd lost weight and I didn't know how to respond."
67. "I have lost weight. I haven't really been eating proper meals."
68. "My jeans are loose but I don't feel any kind of way about it."
69. "I used to care about how I looked. I wore makeup. I had a skincare routine."
70. "Now I wear the same hoodie three days in a row to video meetings."
71. "I keep my camera off most of the time now."
72. "My team probably thinks I'm slacking. Maybe I am."
73. "I had to ask for an extension on a project last week. I've never asked for an extension."
74. "My manager was kind about it, which somehow made me feel worse."
75. "I don't want pity. I want to be the person I was three years ago."
76. "Do you think people can actually go back to who they were before something broke them?"
77. "Sometimes I think David didn't just leave me, he took a version of me with him."
78. "I saw a couple holding hands on Broadway last Friday and I had to sit down on a bench."
79. "I cried in public like a crazy person. A woman asked if I needed help."
80. "I told her I was fine. I'm always telling people I'm fine."
81. "I don't even know what fine means anymore."
82. "When you ask me how I am at the start of these sessions, I never know how to answer honestly."
83. "I default to 'okay' because the truth is too complicated."
84. "The truth is I feel like I'm watching my life happen from behind glass."
85. "I had a moment of joy yesterday, briefly. Mochi did something funny."
86. "And then I felt guilty for laughing. Like I haven't earned the right to feel good."
87. "Is that normal? To feel guilty about feeling better?"
88. "I keep waiting for something to feel like the old me."
89. "I tried going for a run on Sunday because everyone says exercise helps."
90. "I made it three blocks before I turned around and went home."
91. "I haven't been to my book club in four months. They stopped inviting me."
92. "I don't blame them. I'd stop inviting me too."
93. "What if I never feel like myself again? What if this is just who I am now?"
94. "I'm scared that I'm wasting my thirties being sad."
95. "Everyone says these are the best years and I'm just surviving them."
96. "I want to want things again. Right now I don't want anything."
97. "Except maybe to sleep. I want to sleep a lot."
98. "But then when I do sleep, I have these vivid dreams that exhaust me."
99. "I don't know what I expected from therapy. I think I wanted you to fix me faster."
100. "But I'm here. I came today. That has to count for something, right?"
